reasons.vendor: NPX-1245 (rule #59): RAM 6144 / 2 vCPU = EVE veos.yml. The platform applied them (argv -m 6144 -smp 2) but NO boot proof: the library only holds the unsupported full vEOS 4.14.x, not a vEOS-lab image (open blocker in NPX-1245).
reasons.day0_channel:
SUPPORTED VARIANT = vEOS-lab only (2026-08-22, the project owner decision, NPX-516): matches
EVE-NG's own veos.yml (no cdrom line at all, boots straight from hd) and Arista's own
support boundary - vEOS-lab is the only Arista-virtualization-supported build, it is
self-booting (Aboot embedded in the primary disk). Full production vEOS (needs a
separate external Aboot boot ISO - confirmed live: an imported "veos-4.14.5F" full-vEOS
image's MBR boot code is genuinely all zero, and it hangs indefinitely - zero console
output on VGA or serial, CPU pegged - at the post-Aboot kernel handoff under plain KVM)
is explicitly NOT supported here, same as EVE-NG. Earlier revisions of this profile
(2026-08-20) added an extra_disks=["cdrom.iso"]/boot_order=["cdrom","hd"] requirement to
try to boot that full-vEOS build - removed: wrong scope, not a netplex bug to fix.
day0_channel="veos" (2026-07-29): qemu-nbd-mounts the node's own primary disk and
writes startup-config directly onto it pre-boot - vEOS-lab's Aboot bootloader has no
external CD-ROM/config-drive convention, unlike CVAC/Juniper/VyOS (see
day0_channels.py's VeosChannel docstring).
